# Pymageddon

> Pymageddon is a free-to-play, browser-based MMO survival game that simulates a living ecosystem with real predator-prey dynamics. Plants, herbivores and predators all need food to survive, so populations rise and crash like in nature. Players either steer a creature live (keyboard or touch joystick) or deploy a sandboxed Python bot that drives it every tick and competes on a public leaderboard.

Key facts:

- Website: {{ site_url }}/
- Price: free. No download required; works on desktop and mobile browsers.
- Genres: MMO, survival, strategy, programming game, ecosystem simulation.
- Source code: https://github.com/snow884/pymageddon

## Pages

- [Home]({{ site_url }}/): game overview and gameplay video
- [Play]({{ site_url }}/play): live game client (requires a login or a guest account)
- [Start a game]({{ site_url }}/start_game_page): choose to play as a guest or log in
- [Write a bot]({{ site_url }}/create_bot_page): editor for deploying a Python bot
- [Species explorer]({{ site_url }}/explorer): every animal, plant and object in the world, with live populations
- [World map]({{ site_url }}/world_map): live map of the whole world and population history charts
- [Players]({{ site_url }}/players): leaderboard of players and bot families

## HTTP API

- [OpenAPI schema]({{ site_url }}/openapi.json): machine-readable description of every endpoint
- [Interactive API docs]({{ site_url }}/docs): Swagger UI

To get an access token, call `POST /token` with `{"is_guest": true}` for a guest account, or with `{"username": "...", "password": "..."}` for a registered account. Then send the token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Create a registered account with `POST /create_player` and the body `{"username", "password", "verify_password"}`.

| Method | Path | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| POST | /new_game | Join the world as a player creature |
| POST | /create_bot | Deploy bot code `{"code_str": "..."}` and spectate it |
| POST | /control | Send held keys `{"ArrowUp","ArrowDown","ArrowLeft","ArrowRight"}` (booleans) |
| GET | /get_map | Visible map window: tiles, objects, particles, player status |
| GET | /score | Your scores and ranks |
| POST | /end_game | Leave the current game |
| GET | /me | Name of the authenticated user |

The world runs in epochs of about 0.33 s. `/get_map` returns `global_params.status` (`stopped` or `running`) and `time_left` until the next epoch.

## Bot language

Bot code is a safe subset of Python, evaluated once per tick in a sandbox that is limited to 1000 steps. Set the variable `intent` to one of the following:

- `"MOVE_FORWARD"`
- `"ROTATE_UP"`
- `"ROTATE_RIGHT"`
- `"ROTATE_DOWN"`
- `"ROTATE_LEFT"`

If you leave `intent` unset (`None`), the bot idles.

Allowed syntax and functions:

- Allowed syntax: assignments, `if` / `elif` / `else`, `global`, arithmetic, comparisons, `and` / `or` / `not`, `in` / `not in`, list / tuple / dict literals, and indexing. Loops, imports, attribute access, `def` and `print` are rejected.
- `and` / `or` evaluate both sides, so nest `if` statements instead of writing `x and x["y"]`.
- `parent_object` is a dict with `x`, `y` and `rotation` (`"UP"`, `"RIGHT"`, `"DOWN"` or `"LEFT"`) describing your creature. The y axis points down.
- `find_nearest_xy(x, y, type_name_or_list, rad=10)` returns the nearest object of that type (for example `"Grass"`, `"Cow"` or `["Fox", "Badger"]`) as `{x, y, rotation}`, or `None`.
- `random_randint(a, b)` and `random_choice(list)` return random values.
- `get_index(list, i)` and `set_index(list, i, value)` read and write list elements.
- Every variable persists between ticks. Reading a variable that has never been assigned is an error, so declare it with `global name` first; this initializes it to `None` on the first tick.
- Any error discards the bot's variables, and the creature idles for that tick.

Example: walk toward the nearest grass and wander when none is in range.

```python
global steps
if not steps:
    steps = 0
steps = steps + 1
me = parent_object
target = find_nearest_xy(me["x"], me["y"], "Grass")
intent = "MOVE_FORWARD"
if target:
    if target["x"] > me["x"]:
        want = "RIGHT"
    elif target["x"] < me["x"]:
        want = "LEFT"
    elif target["y"] < me["y"]:
        want = "UP"
    else:
        want = "DOWN"
    if me["rotation"] != want:
        intent = "ROTATE_" + want
elif steps % 5 == 0:
    intent = random_choice(["ROTATE_UP", "ROTATE_RIGHT", "ROTATE_DOWN", "ROTATE_LEFT"])
```
